notes:
SEGMENT SCOPE: districts (788, sourced from Wikipedia 'List of districts in India', cross-checked against lgdirectory.gov.in's live homepage dashboard which shows 784 officially LGD-coded districts as of 2026-09-25 - the ~4 extra are newly announced districts, e.g. Goa's Kushavati, AP's Polavaram/Markapuram, pending formal LGD coding, kept in with confidence:medium/low and no censusDistrictCode), one national aggregate (in-local-government) with LGD's live totals, per-state/UT Gram Panchayat / Panchayat Samiti / Zila Parishad and Urban Local Body aggregate tier entities, and the 10 Sixth Schedule autonomous/traditional councils (Assam's BTC/KAAC/DHATC, Tripura's TTAADC, Mizoram's 3 LADCs, Meghalaya's 3 ADCs).

KNOWN GAPS (declared rather than guessed):
1. Administrative divisions (revenue divisions/sambhag/commissionerates) inside states with them (UP, Bihar, MP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Assam, etc.) were NOT modeled as separate 'division' entities; all districts parent directly to their st-<code>. This was a scope cut under time budget, not a missing-source issue - it should be picked up in a follow-up pass.
2. State-wise seat counts for Gram Panchayats / Panchayat Samitis / Zila Parishads (and the Municipality / Nagar Panchayat split of Urban Local Bodies, per state) could not be sourced. lgdirectory.gov.in's interactive statewise/district query reports (globalViewStatewiseLocalBody.do, and the 'Download Directory' PRI/ULB/TLB-by-state reports) sit behind a CAPTCHA ('Get Data' button requires entering a CAPTCHA code); bypassing CAPTCHAs is outside permitted tooling for this session, so those numbers were left out rather than estimated. Only the *national* totals, which are shown un-gated on the LGD homepage's live dashboard, were captured (on in-local-government). This session's shared WebSearch budget (200/200) was also exhausted by sibling segments before an alternate state-wise secondary source (e.g. a Ministry of Panchayati Raj / State of Panchayati Raj Report PDF) could be located - a good next step for whoever picks this gap up.
3. officialUrl (district NIC portal) was not populated for any district: verifying that each <name>.nic.in guess actually resolves for ~788 districts was out of budget for this pass, and guessing URLs without verification would violate the 'never invent a URL' quality bar.
4. population2011/population2021 and areaKm2 on district entities come from a single source (Wikipedia's 'List of districts in India', itself citing Census 2011 / state gazettes / press reports for the newest districts) and were not independently cross-checked per-district; confidence is marked 'medium' throughout for that reason. A few very recently carved districts (e.g. Kushavati, Goa) may still be at an announced/notified stage rather than fully operational - flagged individually.
5. Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram are constitutionally exempt from Part IX (Panchayats) under Article 243-M, so no Gram Panchayat/Panchayat Samiti/Zila Parishad entities exist for them; Nagaland's own village-council system (Nagaland Village and Area Councils Act) is out of the explicit Sixth Schedule list given in the task brief and is not modeled here - a declared gap. CORRECTED during verification (2026-09-25): Lakshadweep was wrongly left out of this same bucket in the original pass even though it is NOT exempt - it has a sourced two-tier Panchayati Raj (10 Village Panchayats + 1 District Panchayat); those two entities have now been added. Chandigarh and Delhi remain undermodeled and NOT confirmed exempt: Delhi has ~300 villages and is covered by the Delhi Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, and Chandigarh has a small rural population (~3% per the 2011 census, including at least one named village) that may fall under Punjab's Panchayati Raj Act as extended to the UT - but current gram panchayat/seat counts for both could not be sourced with the tools available this pass, so no entities were added for them. Flagged for a follow-up pass rather than guessed.
6. Jammu & Kashmir's local government layer (District Development Councils, elected 2020, sit alongside/atop the older Panchayati Raj structure) is represented with the same generic gram-panchayats/panchayat-samitis/zila-parishads pattern as other states; the DDC layer specifically was not modeled as a distinct entity - a further gap given J&K's non-standard structure.

entities.name: Local Government of India (aggregate)
entities.description: The national aggregate of all rural and urban local self-government bodies in India: village, intermediate and district-level Panchayati Raj Institutions (Part IX) and urban local bodies (Part IXA), as tracked in the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's Local Government Directory (LGD).
entities.legalBasis: Constitution of India, Part IX (Panchayats) and Part IXA (Municipalities), inserted by the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992
entities.notes: Live counters read from the lgdirectory.gov.in homepage dashboard on 2026-09-25 (public, no login/CAPTCHA required for this summary view). Urban Local Bodies total (5051) does not exactly equal the sum of the three listed categories (273+2006+2420=4699); the ~352 balance is presumably other ULB categories (e.g. cantonment boards, notified area committees, industrial townships) not broken out on the dashboard. Districts total here (784) is LGD's officially-coded count; our district entity list below (788) is slightly higher because it follows Wikipedia's 'List of districts in India' and includes a handful of newly announced/renamed districts (e.g. Goa's Kushavati, Andhra Pradesh's Polavaram and Markapuram) that a few states have notified but that had not yet received formal LGD codes as of this fetch — flagged individually via a missing censusDistrictCode/low confidence where applicable.

Attempted to verify Delhi/Chandigarh Panchayati Raj status; found Delhi has ~300 villages under the Delhi Panchayati Raj Act and Chandigarh has a small rural population, but could not source exact current gram panchayat/seat counts for either with the tools available (browser tools disallowed; WebSearch budget was already exhausted by sibling segment agents sharing this session's quota) - left unadded rather than guessed, and the gap is now explicitly flagged rather than silently implied to be a constitutional exemption.
